limits_and_continuity.concept: Formal definition of limit; continuity requires limit equals function value at point.
limits_and_continuity.formula: lim(x→a) f(x) = L; f continuous at a if lim(x→a) f(x) = f(a)
conditions: limit must exist from both sides
function defined at point for continuity
common_traps: confusing limit existing with function being defined
assuming differentiability implies continuity but not vice versa

differentiation.concept: Rate of change of function; derivative as slope of tangent to curve.
conditions: function must be continuous; continuity does not guarantee differentiability
common_traps: misapplying chain rule in composite functions
forgetting implicit differentiation steps

integration.concept: Antiderivative and area under curve; fundamental theorem connects differentiation and integration.
conditions: integrand must be Riemann integrable on interval
common_traps: forgetting constant of integration
wrong limits after substitution

taylor_series.concept: Representation of a smooth function as infinite power series about a point.
conditions: function must be infinitely differentiable in neighborhood of expansion point
common_traps: using Taylor series outside radius of convergence
truncating too early in approximations

partial_derivatives.concept: Derivative of multivariable function with respect to one variable, holding others constant.
conditions: Clairaut's theorem requires mixed partials to be continuous
common_traps: treating other variables as constants when they are implicitly dependent

jacobian.concept: Matrix of all first-order partial derivatives; determinant measures volume scaling in coordinate transformations.
applications: change of variables in multiple integrals
conditions: Jacobian must be non-zero for valid transformation (invertibility)
common_traps: forgetting absolute value of Jacobian
inverting Jacobian incorrectly

multiple_integrals.concept: Extension of integration to functions of several variables over 2D/3D domains.
conditions: Fubini's theorem valid when function is continuous on bounded region
common_traps: incorrect limits in iterated integrals
not accounting for Jacobian in coordinate changes

gradient.concept: Vector operator giving direction and magnitude of maximum rate of increase of scalar field.
conditions: scalar field must be differentiable
common_traps: confusing gradient direction with field direction for negative potentials

divergence.concept: Scalar measure of net outward flux of a vector field per unit volume at a point.
conditions: field must be differentiable
common_traps: confusing divergence (scalar) with gradient (vector)

curl.concept: Vector measure of rotation or circulation of a vector field at a point.
conditions: field must be differentiable; zero curl implies conservative field in simply connected domain
common_traps: assuming zero curl globally from zero curl at a point
forgetting domain topology for conservative field

divergence_theorem.concept: Relates volume integral of divergence to surface integral of flux over closed surface.
applications: deriving Gauss's law in integral form
conditions: A must be continuously differentiable in volume V
common_traps: using open instead of closed surface
wrong sign for outward normal

stokes_theorem.concept: Relates line integral of vector field around closed loop to surface integral of curl over bounded surface.
conditions: surface bounded by curve C; field must be smooth on surface
common_traps: wrong orientation of surface relative to curve
using Stokes for non-smooth fields

greens_theorem.concept: 2D special case of Stokes' theorem relating line integral to double integral over enclosed region.
conditions: P, Q must have continuous partial derivatives in D
common_traps: wrong orientation of boundary curve

separable_equations.concept: ODE where variables can be separated to each side and integrated independently.
conditions: g(y) ≠ 0 for separation to be valid
common_traps: dividing by zero when g(y)=0 (missing singular solutions)

linear_first_order.concept: ODE of form dy/dx + P(x)y = Q(x); solved via integrating factor.
linear_first_order.formula: Integrating factor μ(x) = e^(∫P(x)dx); solution: y = (1/μ)∫μQ dx
conditions: P(x) and Q(x) must be continuous
common_traps: incorrect computation of integrating factor exponent

constant_coefficient_homogeneous.concept: ODE of form ay'' + by' + cy = 0; solution depends on roots of characteristic equation.
constant_coefficient_homogeneous.formula: ar² + br + c = 0; y = e^(r1x), e^(r2x) (distinct real), xe^(rx) (repeated), e^(αx)cos(βx)/sin(βx) (complex)
conditions: coefficients must be constant
common_traps: missing second solution in repeated root case (xe^rx term)

method_of_undetermined_coefficients.concept: Method to find particular solution of non-homogeneous ODE by guessing form based on driving term.
method_of_undetermined_coefficients.formula: y_p = A·(trial function matching RHS form)
conditions: driving function must be polynomial, exponential, sine, cosine, or product thereof
common_traps: not modifying trial function when it duplicates homogeneous solution (resonance case)

variation_of_parameters.concept: General method to find particular solution using known homogeneous solutions.
variation_of_parameters.formula: y_p = u1(x)y1 + u2(x)y2; u1' = -y2·f/W, u2' = y1·f/W where W is Wronskian
conditions: two linearly independent homogeneous solutions must be known
common_traps: computing Wronskian incorrectly
forgetting to divide by leading coefficient

sturm_liouville_theory.concept: Framework for second-order linear eigenvalue ODEs; guarantees orthogonal eigenfunctions.
conditions: p(x) > 0, w(x) > 0 on interval; appropriate boundary conditions
common_traps: confusing eigenvalues with energy eigenvalues without proper mapping
neglecting weight function in orthogonality integrals

legendre_polynomials.concept: Solutions of Legendre's equation; arise in problems with spherical symmetry.
legendre_polynomials.formula: (1-x²)y'' - 2xy' + l(l+1)y = 0; P_l(x) via Rodrigues' formula: P_l(x) = (1/2^l l!) d^l/dx^l (x²-1)^l
conditions: regular solutions exist only for l = 0,1,2,... (integer)
common_traps: confusing Legendre polynomials with associated Legendre functions

bessel_functions.concept: Solutions of Bessel's equation; arise in problems with cylindrical symmetry.
components: Bessel functions of first kind J_n
conditions: J_n regular at origin; Y_n singular at origin
common_traps: using Y_n in problems requiring regularity at origin

hermite_polynomials.concept: Solutions of Hermite's equation; arise as wavefunctions of quantum harmonic oscillator.
conditions: orthogonal with weight e^(-x²) on (-∞,∞)
common_traps: two conventions for Hermite polynomials (physicists' vs probabilists')

spherical_harmonics.concept: Angular part of solutions to Laplace's equation in spherical coordinates; eigenfunctions of L² and Lz.
spherical_harmonics.formula: Y_l^m(θ,φ) = N_lm P_l^m(cosθ) e^(imφ); L²Y_l^m = ℏ²l(l+1)Y_l^m
common_traps: confusing l and m ranges
phase conventions (Condon-Shortley)

matrix_operations.concept: Matrices as linear maps; operations include addition, multiplication, transposition, inversion.
conditions: multiplication requires compatible dimensions; inverse requires non-zero determinant
common_traps: matrix multiplication is not commutative in general

determinants.concept: Scalar associated with square matrix; zero determinant signals linear dependence / non-invertibility.
determinants.formula: det(A) = Σ_σ sgn(σ) Π_i A_{i,σ(i)} (Leibniz); for 2x2: ad-bc
conditions: determinant defined only for square matrices
common_traps: sign errors in cofactor expansion
expanding along wrong row/column

eigenvalues_and_eigenvectors.concept: Eigenvalue equation Av = λv; eigenvalues are roots of characteristic polynomial.
conditions: diagonalization possible if n linearly independent eigenvectors exist
common_traps: assuming all matrices are diagonalizable
not normalizing eigenvectors

hermitian_and_unitary_matrices.concept: Hermitian: A† = A (real eigenvalues); Unitary: U†U = I (preserves inner product).
hermitian_and_unitary_matrices.formula: A† = (A*)^T; Hermitian eigenvalues real; Unitary eigenvalues on unit circle
conditions: spectral theorem: Hermitian matrix always diagonalizable by unitary matrix
common_traps: confusing Hermitian (complex) with symmetric (real) matrices

basis_and_dimension.concept: Basis is minimal spanning set; dimension is number of basis vectors.
basis_and_dimension.formula: v = Σ c_i e_i (expansion in basis); dim(V) = n for n linearly independent basis vectors
conditions: basis must be linearly independent and span the space
common_traps: confusing spanning set with basis (basis must also be independent)

inner_product_spaces.concept: Vector space with inner product generalizing dot product; enables notions of length and angle.
conditions: inner product must satisfy conjugate symmetry, linearity, positive definiteness
common_traps: forgetting complex conjugate on first argument in physics convention

analytic_functions.concept: Functions of complex variable differentiable in a neighborhood; satisfy Cauchy-Riemann equations.
conditions: partial derivatives must be continuous for C-R to imply analyticity
common_traps: C-R equations necessary but not sufficient without continuity of partials

cauchys_theorem_and_integral_formula.concept: Integral of analytic function over closed contour is zero; value at interior point given by contour integral.
conditions: f must be analytic inside and on C
common_traps: applying Cauchy's theorem when singularities exist inside contour

residue_theorem.concept: Contour integral equals 2πi times sum of residues at poles enclosed.
conditions: contour must enclose poles; Jordan's lemma for semi-circular contours at infinity
common_traps: wrong sign from contour orientation
missing poles at branch points

branch_cuts.concept: Multi-valued complex functions (log, fractional powers) require branch cuts to define single-valued branch.
branch_cuts.formula: log(z) = ln|z| + i·arg(z); principal value: arg ∈ (-π, π]
conditions: choice of branch cut is convention; must be consistent throughout calculation
common_traps: using log without specifying branch; incorrect contour deformation across branch cut

fourier_series.concept: Expansion of periodic function as sum of sinusoids; coefficients from orthogonality.
conditions: Dirichlet conditions: piecewise smooth, finite discontinuities; series converges to average at discontinuity
common_traps: incorrect period normalization
Gibbs overshoot near discontinuities

fourier_transform.concept: Generalizes Fourier series to non-periodic functions; transforms between position/time and momentum/frequency space.
components: delta function as FT of constant
conditions: function must be absolutely integrable (L¹) for FT to exist classically
common_traps: inconsistent conventions for 2π factors
confusing FT and inverse FT

laplace_transform.concept: Integral transform converting ODE into algebraic equation; defined for t≥0.
conditions: f(t) must be of exponential order; s must be in region of convergence
common_traps: incorrect handling of initial conditions
invalid use of final value theorem when poles in RHP

basic_probability.concept: Probability as measure on event space; satisfies Kolmogorov axioms.
conditions: events must be in σ-algebra; probabilities sum to 1
common_traps: confusing P(A|B) with P(B|A) (base rate neglect)

gaussian_distribution.concept: Normal distribution; arises from central limit theorem; symmetric bell curve.
conditions: defined over (-∞, ∞)
common_traps: confusing standard deviation with variance

poisson_distribution.concept: Discrete distribution for rare events in fixed interval; parameter λ = mean number of events.
conditions: events independent; rate constant
common_traps: applying Poisson when events are not independent

error_propagation.concept: How uncertainties in measured quantities combine to give uncertainty in derived quantity.
conditions: errors must be small and uncorrelated for formula to apply
common_traps: adding absolute errors instead of adding in quadrature for independent errors

spherical_coordinates.concept: Coordinate system (r,θ,φ) for 3D space; natural for spherically symmetric problems.
spherical_coordinates.formula: x=r sinθ cosφ, y=r sinθ sinφ, z=r cosθ; dV = r² sinθ dr dθ dφ
components: scale factors h_r=1, h_θ=r, h_φ=r sinθ
gradient, divergence, curl, Laplacian in spherical coords
conditions: r≥0, 0≤θ≤π, 0≤φ<2π; singularity at r=0 and θ=0,π
common_traps: forgetting sin θ in volume element or in Laplacian
θ and φ convention (physics vs math)

cylindrical_coordinates.concept: Coordinate system (ρ,φ,z) for 3D space; natural for cylindrical symmetry.
cylindrical_coordinates.formula: x=ρcosφ, y=ρsinφ, z=z; dV = ρ dρ dφ dz
conditions: ρ≥0; singularity at ρ=0
common_traps: forgetting ρ in area/volume element

laplacian_in_curvilinear_coords.concept: Second-order differential operator generalizing ∇² to curved coordinate systems.
conditions: valid in smooth coordinate systems
common_traps: dropping angular terms for non-spherically-symmetric problems

tensor_definition.concept: Geometric object with components transforming in specific way under coordinate changes.
conditions: transformation law must hold under all coordinate transformations
common_traps: confusing contravariant and covariant index placement

index_notation.concept: Einstein summation convention: repeated index (one up, one down) implies summation.
index_notation.formula: A^μ B_μ = Σ_μ A^μ B_μ (scalar); δ^μ_ν A^ν = A^μ
conditions: each dummy index appears exactly twice (once up, once down)
common_traps: repeating an index more than twice (invalid)

first_law.concept: An object remains at rest or uniform motion unless acted upon by a net external force (inertia).
conditions: valid only in inertial frames
common_traps: applying first law in non-inertial frames without pseudo-forces

second_law.concept: Net force equals rate of change of momentum; for constant mass, F = ma.
applications: equation of motion for all classical systems
conditions: valid in inertial frames; relativistic correction needed at high speeds
common_traps: using F=ma for variable mass (should use F = dp/dt)

third_law.concept: For every action force there is an equal and opposite reaction force on a different body.
conditions: forces act on different objects; does not imply zero acceleration
common_traps: treating action-reaction pair as canceling (they act on different bodies)

conservation_of_momentum.concept: Total momentum of an isolated system is constant; follows from Newton's third law.
conservation_of_momentum.formula: dp_total/dt = F_ext; if F_ext = 0 → p_total = const
conditions: no external forces (or component along direction considered)
common_traps: including internal forces in momentum change calculation

conservation_of_energy.concept: Total mechanical energy conserved when only conservative forces act.
conservation_of_energy.formula: E = KE + PE = const; dE/dt = P_non-conservative
conditions: only conservative forces; no friction or dissipation
common_traps: neglecting non-conservative forces (friction) in energy conservation

elastic_collision.concept: Both momentum and kinetic energy conserved; no deformation or heat generated.
conditions: no energy loss; rigid body approximation
common_traps: using elastic formulas for partially inelastic situations

inelastic_collision.concept: Momentum conserved but kinetic energy not; energy converted to heat/deformation.
conditions: e=1 elastic, e=0 perfectly inelastic, 0<e<1 partially inelastic
common_traps: assuming KE conserved in inelastic collision

generalized_coordinates.concept: Independent coordinates that completely specify system configuration; can be any convenient set.
generalized_coordinates.formula: q = (q₁, q₂, ..., qₙ); n = degrees of freedom
conditions: coordinates must be independent after applying constraints
common_traps: using more coordinates than degrees of freedom (over-specification)

principle_of_least_action.concept: Physical trajectory extremizes the action integral S = ∫L dt.
conditions: variations must vanish at endpoints
common_traps: confusing extremal (could be maximum) with minimum action

euler_lagrange_equations.concept: Differential equations for generalized coordinates obtained from least action principle.
applications: field equations in classical field theory
conditions: L must be differentiable in qᵢ and q̇ᵢ
common_traps: incorrect computation of total time derivative d/dt(∂L/∂q̇)

conditions: rigid massless rod; small angle for SHM approximation
common_traps: using small angle approximation outside valid range (θ < ~10°)

central_force_problem.concept: Two-body problem reducible to one-body problem in center of mass frame; L conserved.
central_force_problem.formula: L = (1/2)μṙ² + (1/2)μr²θ̇² - V(r); reduced mass μ = m₁m₂/(m₁+m₂)
conditions: force depends only on |r|
common_traps: forgetting to use reduced mass in two-body problem

noethers_theorem.concept: Every continuous symmetry of the Lagrangian corresponds to a conserved quantity.
noethers_theorem.formula: If L invariant under q → q + εK, conserved quantity Q = Σ (∂L/∂q̇ᵢ)Kᵢ
conditions: symmetry must be continuous (Lie group)
common_traps: applying Noether to discrete symmetries (they don't give conserved currents via this theorem)

cyclic_coordinates.concept: Coordinate absent from L (∂L/∂qᵢ = 0) implies conjugate momentum pᵢ is conserved.
applications: φ cyclic in central force → Lz conserved
conditions: coordinate must be absent from L (not just from T or V separately)
common_traps: identifying cyclic coordinate in V while T still depends on it through kinetic coupling

legendre_transformation.concept: Transforms Lagrangian (q, q̇) description to Hamiltonian (q, p) phase space description.
legendre_transformation.formula: H(q, p, t) = Σ pᵢq̇ᵢ - L; pᵢ = ∂L/∂q̇ᵢ
conditions: Hessian ∂²L/∂q̇ᵢ∂q̇ⱼ must be non-singular for Legendre transform to be invertible
common_traps: algebraic errors in eliminating q̇ in favor of p

hamiltons_equations.concept: First-order equations of motion in phase space equivalent to Newton's second law.
applications: canonical quantization (replace Poisson brackets with commutators)
conditions: canonical coordinates must satisfy Poisson bracket relations
common_traps: sign error in ṗ equation (minus sign)

poisson_brackets.concept: Binary operation on phase space functions encoding symplectic structure and evolution.
conditions: valid on smooth phase space functions
common_traps: sign errors in Poisson bracket calculation

simple_harmonic_oscillator.concept: System with restoring force proportional to displacement; sinusoidal motion.
simple_harmonic_oscillator.formula: ẍ + ω₀²x = 0; x(t) = A cos(ω₀t + φ); ω₀ = √(k/m)
applications: small oscillations of any stable equilibrium
conditions: linear restoring force; valid near stable equilibrium
common_traps: confusing angular frequency ω with frequency f = ω/2π

damped_oscillator.concept: SHO with velocity-proportional damping; amplitude decays exponentially.
damped_oscillator.formula: ẍ + 2γẋ + ω₀²x = 0; underdamped: x = Ae^(-γt)cos(ω_d t + φ); ω_d = √(ω₀²-γ²)
conditions: linear damping assumed
common_traps: confusing decay rate γ with damping coefficient b (F = -bv, γ = b/2m)

driven_oscillator_and_resonance.concept: Forced oscillator at steady state; amplitude peaks near natural frequency (resonance).
driven_oscillator_and_resonance.formula: x_steady = F₀/m / √((ω₀²-ω²)² + 4γ²ω²) cos(ωt-δ); resonance at ω_res = √(ω₀²-2γ²)
conditions: linear system; damping present prevents infinite amplitude at resonance
common_traps: resonance frequency ω_res ≠ ω₀ when damping present

normal_modes.concept: Collective oscillations of coupled system where all parts oscillate at same frequency.
conditions: small oscillations about equilibrium; linear approximation
common_traps: not transforming to normal coordinates when solving initial value problem

effective_potential.concept: 1D equivalent potential including centrifugal barrier; determines radial motion.
conditions: only for central force problem with conserved angular momentum
common_traps: treating centrifugal term as a real force rather than fictitious

first_law.concept: Planets orbit in ellipses with the Sun at one focus.
first_law.formula: r = a(1-e²)/(1 + e cosθ); e = eccentricity
conditions: inverse-square gravity; two-body problem with reduced mass
common_traps: confusing semi-major with semi-minor axis in energy formula

second_law.concept: Equal areas swept in equal times; consequence of angular momentum conservation.
conditions: any central force (not just gravity)
common_traps: assuming orbital speed is constant

third_law.concept: Square of orbital period proportional to cube of semi-major axis.
conditions: strictly for inverse-square gravity; approximate for m₁ >> m₂
common_traps: using T² ∝ a³ without correct proportionality constant

orbit_types.concept: Orbit shape determined by energy and eccentricity: bound (E<0, ellipse), marginally bound (E=0, parabola), unbound (E>0, hyperbola).
conditions: inverse-square force (1/r² gravity)
common_traps: applying orbit energy formula to non-inverse-square force

postulates.concept: Physics laws same in all inertial frames; speed of light c constant in all inertial frames.
postulates.formula: c = 2.998 × 10⁸ m/s; invariant under Lorentz transformations
conditions: special relativity; no gravity (flat spacetime)
common_traps: assuming simultaneity is absolute

lorentz_transformations.concept: Coordinate transformation between inertial frames; mixes space and time.
lorentz_transformations.formula: t' = γ(t - vx/c²); x' = γ(x - vt); γ = 1/√(1-β²); β = v/c
conditions: relative velocity v along x-axis; inertial frames
common_traps: applying time dilation formula to non-proper time intervals

time_dilation.concept: Moving clock runs slow; proper time τ < coordinate time t.
conditions: Δτ is time in rest frame of moving clock
common_traps: applying wrong frame for proper time

length_contraction.concept: Moving rod appears shorter along direction of motion.
conditions: contraction only along direction of motion
common_traps: applying contraction to transverse dimensions

relativistic_energy_momentum.concept: Relativistic energy includes rest energy; 4-momentum is Lorentz covariant.
relativistic_energy_momentum.formula: E = γmc²; p = γmv; E² = (pc)² + (mc²)²; E = mc² for rest
conditions: valid for all speeds; Newtonian limit at v << c
common_traps: using KE = (1/2)mv² relativistically
confusing relativistic momentum with p=mv

moment_of_inertia.concept: Rotational analog of mass; measures resistance to angular acceleration.
moment_of_inertia.formula: I = Σmᵢrᵢ² (discrete); I = ∫r²dm (continuous); I = Icm + Md² (parallel axis)
conditions: axis must be specified; perpendicular axis theorem valid only for planar bodies
common_traps: applying perpendicular axis theorem to 3D objects
wrong distance in parallel axis theorem

euler_equations.concept: Equations of motion for rigid body rotation in body-fixed frame.
conditions: axes must be principal axes
common_traps: using Euler equations in non-principal axis frame

equation_of_continuity.concept: Mass conservation for fluid flow; density flux through surface equals rate of density change.
conditions: continuum approximation valid
common_traps: assuming all fluids incompressible (fails for gases at high speed)

bernoullis_theorem.concept: Conservation of energy along streamline in ideal fluid flow.
conditions: steady, incompressible, inviscid flow along streamline
common_traps: applying Bernoulli across streamlines
ignoring viscosity when it matters

coulombs_law.concept: Force between two point charges inversely proportional to square of separation.
applications: building up field from charge distribution
conditions: point charges or spherically symmetric distributions; charges at rest
common_traps: forgetting vector nature (direction) of force

electric_field.concept: Force per unit positive test charge; vector field defined at every point in space.
conditions: test charge must be small enough not to disturb source distribution
common_traps: confusing direction of E for negative source charge

gausss_law.concept: Total electric flux through closed surface equals enclosed charge divided by ε₀.
applications: field of spherical, cylindrical, planar charge distributions
conditions: most useful when high symmetry allows E to be pulled out of integral
common_traps: using Gauss's law for asymmetric distributions without symmetry argument

electric_potential.concept: Scalar field whose negative gradient gives electric field; potential energy per unit charge.
conditions: reference point must be specified (usually V=0 at infinity)
common_traps: sign error: V decreases in direction of E field

laplaces_and_poissons_equations.concept: PDEs for electric potential; Laplace: ∇²V = 0 (no charges); Poisson: ∇²V = -ρ/ε₀.
conditions: unique solution given appropriate boundary conditions
common_traps: not specifying boundary conditions (solution not unique)

multipole_expansion.concept: Expansion of potential at large distances in terms of multipole moments: monopole, dipole, quadrupole.
conditions: valid for r >> size of charge distribution
common_traps: dipole moment is origin-dependent unless monopole Q=0

conductors.concept: In electrostatic equilibrium: E=0 inside conductor, charges on surface, surface is equipotential.
conductors.formula: E_surface = σ/ε₀ n̂; V = const inside and on surface
conditions: electrostatic equilibrium (static charges)
common_traps: applying conductor properties to static non-metallic materials

method_of_images.concept: Replace boundary conditions by fictitious image charges to satisfy Laplace equation.
method_of_images.formula: For point charge q at distance d from grounded plane: image charge -q at distance d behind plane
conditions: image charge method valid only for specific geometries
common_traps: placing image charge in physical region (wrong side of boundary)

dielectrics.concept: Insulating material that gets polarized in electric field; reduces effective field.
dielectrics.formula: D = ε₀E + P = εE; P = ε₀χₑE; ε = ε₀(1+χₑ) = ε₀εᵣ
conditions: linear, isotropic dielectric assumed unless stated
common_traps: confusing E and D fields at dielectric interfaces

boundary_conditions_em.concept: Conditions on E, D, B, H fields at interface between two media.
boundary_conditions_em.formula: E₁ₜ = E₂ₜ; D₁ₙ - D₂ₙ = σ_free; B₁ₙ = B₂ₙ; H₁ₜ - H₂ₜ = K_free
applications: reflection and refraction of EM waves
conditions: applies at sharp interface between two media
common_traps: using wrong boundary condition (E or D) at interface

biot_savart_law.concept: Magnetic field produced by steady current element; inverse square in distance.
biot_savart_law.formula: dB = (μ₀/4π) I dl × r̂ / r²; B = (μ₀/4π) ∫ I dl × r̂ / r²
conditions: steady (DC) currents only; magnetostatics
common_traps: wrong direction from cross product; forgetting to integrate over full current path

amperes_law.concept: Line integral of B around closed loop equals μ₀ times enclosed current.
amperes_law.formula: ∮ B·dl = μ₀ I_enc; ∇×B = μ₀J (differential form, magnetostatics)
conditions: most useful with high symmetry; requires steady currents in magnetostatics form
common_traps: including displacement current from Ampere's law (that's Maxwell's generalization)

magnetic_vector_potential.concept: Vector potential A such that B = ∇×A; gauge freedom in choosing A.
conditions: A is not uniquely defined; gauge choice must be specified
common_traps: treating A as directly physical without accounting for gauge

faradays_law.concept: Changing magnetic flux induces EMF in loop; basis of electromagnetic induction.
conditions: valid for any loop (stationary or moving)
common_traps: sign error: Lenz's law (induced current opposes change)

maxwell_equations.concept: Complete set of four equations governing electromagnetic fields; predict EM waves.
conditions: in vacuum; modify for media using D, H, ε, μ
common_traps: forgetting displacement current in high-frequency AC problems

plane_waves.concept: Transverse oscillating E and B fields propagating at speed c; E⊥B⊥k.
plane_waves.formula: E = E₀ cos(k·r - ωt); B = (k̂×E)/c; c = 1/√(μ₀ε₀); ω = ck
components: E and B amplitudes related by c
conditions: plane wave approximation valid far from source
common_traps: B amplitude is E₀/c, not E₀; confusing E₀ as field magnitude with wave amplitude

poynting_vector.concept: Energy flux (power per unit area) of EM field; direction of energy propagation.
conditions: valid for fields in vacuum or simple media
common_traps: using instantaneous S rather than time-averaged for intensity calculations

reflection_and_refraction.concept: EM wave behavior at interface between media with different ε; Fresnel equations give amplitudes.
reflection_and_refraction.formula: Snell's law: n₁sinθ₁ = n₂sinθ₂; n = c/v = √(εᵣμᵣ)
conditions: interface assumed planar and sharp; plane wave incidence
common_traps: using scalar Snell's law without polarization-dependent amplitude coefficients

waves_in_dispersive_media.concept: In dispersive media, phase velocity depends on frequency; group velocity ≠ phase velocity.
waves_in_dispersive_media.formula: v_phase = ω/k; v_group = dω/dk; skin depth δ = √(2/μσω)
conditions: linear response assumed; valid for weak fields
common_traps: confusing phase and group velocity for signal transmission speed

self_inductance.concept: Flux through a circuit due to its own current; opposes changes in current.
self_inductance.formula: Φ = LI; EMF = -L dI/dt; L = μ₀N²A/l (solenoid)
conditions: linear media assumed
common_traps: forgetting the factor N (flux linkage vs flux per turn)

mutual_inductance.concept: EMF induced in one circuit by changing current in another; M₁₂ = M₂₁.
conditions: reciprocity M₁₂ = M₂₁ holds for linear media
common_traps: sign error in induced EMF direction

youngs_double_slit.concept: Two coherent point sources produce sinusoidal interference pattern on screen.
youngs_double_slit.formula: Δ = d sinθ; bright: Δ = mλ; dark: Δ = (m+1/2)λ; fringe width β = λD/d
conditions: coherent sources; d << D (screen distance); monochromatic light
common_traps: using degrees instead of radians in small angle approximation

thin_film_interference.concept: Interference between rays reflected from top and bottom surfaces of thin film.
thin_film_interference.formula: Optical path difference = 2nt cosθ_r (±λ/2 for phase shift at denser medium reflection)
components: phase shift on reflection from denser medium (λ/2 shift)
conditions: coherent light; film uniform thickness
common_traps: forgetting phase reversal (λ/2 shift) when reflecting from denser medium

single_slit.concept: Diffraction pattern from single slit; central maximum flanked by weaker secondary maxima.
single_slit.formula: I(θ) = I₀ (sin α/α)²; α = πa sinθ/λ; minima: a sinθ = mλ (m≠0)
conditions: Fraunhofer: far field (L >> a²/λ)
common_traps: minima at a sinθ = mλ not maxima

diffraction_grating.concept: Multiple-slit interference produces sharp principal maxima; high resolving power.
diffraction_grating.formula: d sinθ = mλ (principal maxima); resolving power R = mN
conditions: N slits with equal spacing d; coherent illumination
common_traps: confusing resolving power with dispersion

rayleigh_criterion.concept: Two point sources just resolved when central maximum of one falls on first minimum of other.
conditions: Fraunhofer diffraction; incoherent sources
common_traps: factor 1.22 specific to circular aperture; not for slits

linear_polarization.concept: Electric field oscillates in a single plane; produced by selective absorption or reflection.
conditions: completely polarized input light for Malus's law
common_traps: Malus's law applies to completely polarized light; unpolarized light halved by first polarizer

circular_and_elliptical_polarization.concept: Superposition of two orthogonal linear polarizations with phase difference; tip of E traces ellipse/circle.
circular_and_elliptical_polarization.formula: Ex = E₀cosωt; Ey = E₀cos(ωt+δ); circular: δ=±π/2, |Ex|=|Ey|
conditions: monochromatic coherent superposition of two polarizations
common_traps: confusing right vs left circular polarization conventions (physics vs optics)

brewsters_angle.concept: Angle at which reflected light is completely linearly polarized (p-polarization not reflected).
brewsters_angle.formula: tan θ_B = n₂/n₁; at θ_B: reflected and transmitted beams perpendicular
conditions: dielectric interface; non-absorbing medium
common_traps: at Brewster's angle, only s-polarization is reflected, not both

thin_lens_equation.concept: Relates object distance, image distance, and focal length for thin lens.
conditions: thin lens approximation (thickness << f)
common_traps: sign convention errors (varies by convention used)

lens_combinations.concept: Power of thin lenses in contact adds; effective focal length from combination.
conditions: paraxial approximation
common_traps: using thin lens formula for thick lens combinations

de_broglie_hypothesis.concept: Particles have associated wavelength λ = h/p; matter exhibits wave properties.
conditions: quantum regime: λ comparable to system size
common_traps: using non-relativistic momentum for high-energy particles

uncertainty_principle.concept: Conjugate variables (position-momentum, energy-time) cannot both be precisely defined simultaneously.
conditions: uncertainties are standard deviations of quantum distributions, not measurement errors
common_traps: confusing ΔEΔt with position-momentum uncertainty; misinterpreting as measurement disturbance

born_interpretation.concept: Probability density for finding particle at position x is |ψ(x)|².
conditions: ψ must be square integrable (normalizable)
common_traps: confusing ψ (complex amplitude) with |ψ|² (real probability density)

superposition_principle.concept: If ψ₁ and ψ₂ are valid states, so is any linear combination c₁ψ₁ + c₂ψ₂.
conditions: superposition holds before measurement; measurement collapses state
common_traps: probabilities are |cᵢ|² not |cᵢ|, and must be normalized Σ|cᵢ|²=1

time_dependent.concept: Fundamental equation governing quantum state evolution in time.
conditions: non-relativistic; no spin-orbit coupling unless added
common_traps: forgetting factor of i on left side; using ħ=h rather than ħ=h/2π

time_independent.concept: Eigenvalue equation for energy; stationary states have definite energy.
conditions: V must be time-independent for separation of variables
common_traps: not applying correct boundary conditions at potential discontinuities

infinite_square_well.concept: Particle confined between rigid walls; discrete energy spectrum from boundary conditions.
conditions: ψ=0 at walls (infinite potential)
common_traps: n starts at 1, not 0; E ∝ n² not n

finite_square_well.concept: Particle confined in finite potential well; wavefunctions penetrate classically forbidden region (tunneling).
finite_square_well.formula: Inside: ψ ∝ cos/sin(kx); Outside: ψ ∝ e^(±κx); k²=2mE/ℏ², κ²=2m(V₀-E)/ℏ²
components: fewer bound states than infinite well
conditions: E < V₀ for bound states; finite number of bound states
common_traps: applying infinite well energies to finite well
sign error in exponential outside well

energy_levels.concept: Equally spaced energy levels; non-zero ground state (zero-point) energy.
conditions: valid for quadratic potential; generalized to multidimensional harmonic oscillator
common_traps: missing zero-point energy (1/2)ℏω
n=0 is ground state not n=1

ladder_operators.concept: Algebraic operators that raise/lower energy quantum number by 1.
conditions: specific to harmonic oscillator potential
common_traps: confusing a|n⟩ = √n|n-1⟩ vs a†|n⟩ = √(n+1)|n+1⟩

step_potential.concept: Particle encountering abrupt potential jump; quantum reflection even for E>V₀.
conditions: plane wave incident; time-independent
common_traps: quantum reflection: R≠0 even when E>V₀

tunneling_through_barrier.concept: Quantum mechanical transmission through classically forbidden region; exponentially small but nonzero.
tunneling_through_barrier.formula: T ≈ e^(-2κa) for thick barrier; κ = √(2m(V₀-E))/ℏ
conditions: κa >> 1 for thick barrier approximation
common_traps: T is exponentially suppressed but never exactly zero

orbital_angular_momentum.concept: Quantized orbital angular momentum with magnitude √(l(l+1))ℏ and z-component mℏ.
orbital_angular_momentum.formula: L² Y_l^m = l(l+1)ℏ² Y_l^m; Lz Y_l^m = mℏ Y_l^m; l=0,1,2,...; m=-l,...,l
components: angular momentum operators Lx, Ly, Lz
simultaneous eigenstates of L² and Lz
conditions: integer l only for orbital angular momentum
common_traps: confusing l (total) with m (z-component); confusing L² eigenvalue l(l+1) with l²

spin_half.concept: Intrinsic angular momentum with s=1/2; two states spin-up |↑⟩ and spin-down |↓⟩.
conditions: s=1/2 for electrons, protons, neutrons; bosons have integer spin
common_traps: S² eigenvalue is s(s+1)ℏ²= (3/4)ℏ², not (1/2)ℏ²

conditions: 2D representation for spin-1/2 only
common_traps: factor of ℏ/2: S = (ℏ/2)σ, not S = σ

addition_of_angular_momenta.concept: Two angular momenta j₁ and j₂ combine to give total J with |j₁-j₂| ≤ J ≤ j₁+j₂.
conditions: angular momenta must be independent (no interaction needed for addition rule)
common_traps: forgetting triangle inequality for allowed J values

energy_levels.concept: Exact solution of Schrödinger equation for Coulomb potential; discrete bound state energies.
conditions: non-relativistic; ignores spin-orbit coupling, fine structure
common_traps: forgetting factor of n² in denominator (not n)

quantum_numbers.concept: State of H-atom labeled by (n, l, m, ms); n principal, l orbital, m magnetic, ms spin.
conditions: valid for hydrogen-like atoms (single electron)
common_traps: l range: 0 to n-1, not 0 to n

wavefunctions.concept: Hydrogen wavefunctions ψ_nlm = R_nl(r)Y_l^m(θ,φ) factorize into radial and angular parts.
conditions: non-relativistic; ignores fine and hyperfine structure
common_traps: probability density is |ψ|², radial probability is r²|R|²

dirac_notation.concept: Abstract notation with kets |ψ⟩ as state vectors and bras ⟨ψ| as dual vectors.
dirac_notation.formula: ⟨φ|ψ⟩ inner product; |ψ⟩⟨ψ| projection operator; Î = Σ|n⟩⟨n| (completeness)
conditions: Hilbert space; states must be normalizable
common_traps: order matters: ⟨φ|ψ⟩ ≠ ⟨ψ|φ⟩* confusion; |ψ⟩⟨ψ| is operator, ⟨ψ|ψ⟩ is scalar

hermitian_operators_and_observables.concept: Physical observables represented by Hermitian operators; eigenvalues real; eigenstates orthogonal.
conditions: operator must be Hermitian (self-adjoint) for real eigenvalues
common_traps: assuming all operators commute; only commuting observables have simultaneous eigenstates

commutators.concept: Measure of non-commutativity of operators; determines whether observables can be simultaneously measured.
applications: time evolution ([Â,Ĥ] for constants of motion)
conditions: operators must act on same Hilbert space
common_traps: confusing commutator with anticommutator; sign errors

unitary_transformations.concept: Transformations preserving inner product; represent symmetries and time evolution.
unitary_transformations.formula: Û†Û = ÛÛ† = Î; time evolution: Û(t) = e^(-iĤt/ℏ)
conditions: unitarity ensures probability conservation
common_traps: mixing Schrödinger and Heisenberg pictures in same calculation

non_degenerate.concept: Systematic expansion of energy and states in powers of small perturbation H'.
conditions: perturbation small: |⟨m|H'|n⟩| << |E_n^(0)-E_m^(0)|
common_traps: applying non-degenerate formula to degenerate levels

degenerate.concept: For degenerate levels, must diagonalize H' within degenerate subspace to find correct zeroth-order states.
degenerate.formula: Diagonalize H' matrix in degenerate subspace; eigenvalues give first-order corrections
conditions: necessary when two or more states have same unperturbed energy
common_traps: using non-degenerate formula when degeneracy present (energy denominator blows up)

fermi_golden_rule.concept: Transition rate from initial to final state due to time-dependent perturbation; valid at long times.
conditions: valid for slowly varying perturbation at long times; energy conservation enforced
common_traps: using Fermi's golden rule for transitions to discrete final states (must have continuum)

selection_rules.concept: Symmetry constraints that make certain transition matrix elements zero; from commutation of H' with symmetry operators.
conditions: electric dipole approximation (wavelength >> atom size)
common_traps: applying electric dipole selection rules to magnetic dipole transitions

variational_method.concept: Upper bound theorem: ⟨ψ_trial|Ĥ|ψ_trial⟩ ≥ E_ground for any normalized trial state.
conditions: provides upper bound on ground state energy; can extend to excited states
common_traps: poor trial function gives poor bound; not considering symmetry in trial function

zeroth_law.concept: If two systems are each in thermal equilibrium with a third, they are in equilibrium with each other; defines temperature.
conditions: macroscopic systems in equilibrium
common_traps: confusing thermal equilibrium with mechanical equilibrium

first_law.concept: Energy conservation for thermodynamic systems: change in internal energy = heat added minus work done.
first_law.formula: dU = δQ - δW; dU = δQ - PdV (for reversible PV work)
conditions: sign convention: Q positive into system, W positive done by system
common_traps: sign convention errors; treating Q and W as state functions

second_law.concept: Entropy of isolated system never decreases; heat spontaneously flows from hot to cold.
second_law.formula: dS ≥ δQ/T (Clausius inequality); = for reversible, > for irreversible
conditions: applies to macroscopic systems; statistical interpretation in stat mech
common_traps: entropy can decrease locally if compensated by increase elsewhere (2nd law for isolated system)

third_law.concept: Entropy of a perfect crystal approaches zero as T → 0; absolute zero unattainable.
conditions: perfect crystal with non-degenerate ground state
common_traps: systems with ground state degeneracy have residual entropy S = k ln(g₀)

internal_energy.concept: Natural variables: S, V; dU = TdS - PdV.
conditions: U minimized at equilibrium for fixed S,V
common_traps: using U when natural variables are T,P (should use G)

helmholtz_free_energy.concept: F = U - TS; natural variables T, V; minimized at equilibrium for fixed T,V.
helmholtz_free_energy.formula: F = U - TS; dF = -SdT - PdV; S = -(∂F/∂T)_V; P = -(∂F/∂V)_T
conditions: constant T and V
common_traps: using F instead of G at constant pressure

gibbs_free_energy.concept: G = U + PV - TS; natural variables T, P; minimized at equilibrium for fixed T,P.
gibbs_free_energy.formula: G = H - TS; dG = -SdT + VdP; μ = (∂G/∂N)_{T,P}
conditions: constant T and P (most common lab conditions)
common_traps: confusing ΔG with ΔG°; temperature and pressure dependencies

enthalpy.concept: H = U + PV; natural variables S, P; useful for constant-pressure processes.
enthalpy.formula: H = U + PV; dH = TdS + VdP; Q_P = ΔH
conditions: constant pressure
common_traps: using Q = ΔU instead of Q = ΔH at constant pressure

maxwell_relations.concept: Cross-derivative equalities from exactness of thermodynamic potentials; connect measurable quantities.
applications: deriving inaccessible quantities from accessible ones
conditions: valid for simple systems; equilibrium states
common_traps: sign errors; confusing which potential gives which Maxwell relation

clausius_clapeyron.concept: Slope of phase boundary in P-T diagram related to latent heat and volume change.
conditions: two-phase coexistence; equilibrium
common_traps: negative dP/dT for water-ice (anomalous: ΔV < 0)

speed_distribution.concept: Distribution of molecular speeds in ideal gas at temperature T.
conditions: ideal gas in thermal equilibrium; non-relativistic speeds
common_traps: confusing v_p, ⟨v⟩, and v_rms (v_p < ⟨v⟩ < v_rms)

equipartition_theorem.concept: Each quadratic degree of freedom contributes (1/2)kT to average energy.
equipartition_theorem.formula: ⟨E_i⟩ = (1/2)kT per quadratic degree of freedom; U = (f/2)NkT
conditions: classical (high T) limit; breaks down when kT << ℏω (quantum effects)
common_traps: applying equipartition to quantum systems at low T (frozen out modes)

mean_free_path.concept: Average distance molecule travels between collisions.
mean_free_path.formula: λ = 1/(√2 nπd²); mean free time τ = λ/⟨v⟩
conditions: hard sphere model; dilute gas
common_traps: forgetting √2 factor (from relative speed between molecules)

microcanonical_ensemble.concept: Isolated system with fixed E, V, N; all microstates with given energy equally probable.
microcanonical_ensemble.formula: S = k ln Ω; Ω = number of microstates with energy E
conditions: truly isolated system
common_traps: confusing number of microstates Ω with partition function Z

canonical_ensemble.concept: System in thermal contact with heat bath at temperature T; energy fluctuates.
canonical_ensemble.formula: Z = Σ_states e^(-βEₛ); F = -kT ln Z; P_s = e^(-βEs)/Z; β = 1/kT
conditions: weak coupling to heat bath; system size << reservoir
common_traps: dividing by N! for indistinguishable particles (Gibbs paradox correction)

grand_canonical_ensemble.concept: System exchanges both energy and particles with reservoir; T and μ fixed.
grand_canonical_ensemble.formula: Z_G = Σ_{N,s} e^(-β(Eₛ-μN)); Ω = -kT ln Z_G; ⟨N⟩ = -∂Ω/∂μ
conditions: particle exchange allowed; chemical potential controls average particle number
common_traps: forgetting e^(βμN) fugacity factor for each particle

fermi_dirac_distribution.concept: Average occupation of single-particle state for fermions (half-integer spin); obeys Pauli exclusion.
conditions: non-interacting fermions; grand canonical ensemble
common_traps: μ(T) ≠ E_F at T>0; Fermi energy is μ at T=0 only

bose_einstein_distribution.concept: Average occupation of single-particle state for bosons (integer spin); allows multiple occupation.
components: chemical potential μ ≤ 0 (μ < ground state energy)
conditions: μ must be less than minimum single-particle energy to avoid negative occupation
common_traps: μ can equal zero for photons (no particle conservation); negative μ for massive bosons

blackbody_radiation.concept: Thermal radiation spectrum; Planck distribution from quantum treatment of photon gas.
blackbody_radiation.formula: u(ν,T) = (8πhν³/c³)/(e^(hν/kT) - 1); Stefan-Boltzmann: P = σT⁴; Wien: λ_max T = 2.898×10⁻³ m·K
conditions: blackbody: perfect absorber/emitter; real bodies use emissivity ε
common_traps: Rayleigh-Jeans valid only for hν << kT (low frequency)

paramagnetism.concept: Magnetic moments align with external field; entropy and magnetization from partition function.
paramagnetism.formula: Z = (2sinh((J+1/2)βgμ_B B))/sinh(βgμ_B B/2); M = NkT ∂lnZ/∂B; Curie law: χ = C/T
conditions: non-interacting magnetic dipoles; no quantum exchange interaction
common_traps: Langevin (classical) vs Brillouin (quantum) function; applying wrong one

bohr_model.concept: Electrons in circular orbits with quantized angular momentum; predicts H-atom spectrum.
bohr_model.formula: mvr = nℏ; Eₙ = -13.6/n² eV; rₙ = n²a₀
conditions: valid only for hydrogen-like atoms; fails for multi-electron atoms
common_traps: Bohr model is superseded by quantum mechanics; cannot explain fine structure

frank_hertz_experiment.concept: Demonstrates discrete atomic energy levels by electron collision excitation.
frank_hertz_experiment.formula: V_excitation = ΔE/e (threshold voltage for energy transfer)
conditions: monoenergetic electrons; mercury vapor target
common_traps: confusing excitation with ionization potential

pauli_exclusion_principle.concept: No two fermions can occupy the same quantum state simultaneously.
conditions: Identical fermions
common_traps: Applying to bosons

stern_gerlach_experiment.concept: Demonstrates space quantization of angular momentum and existence of electron spin.
conditions: Neutral silver atoms or similar
common_traps: Confusing with Zeeman effect

binding_energy.concept: Energy required to completely disassemble nucleus into free nucleons; B = (Zm_p + Nm_n - M)c².
binding_energy.formula: B/A peaks at iron (most stable); Semi-empirical: B = aᵥA - aₛA^(2/3) - a_C Z(Z-1)/A^(1/3) - aₐ(A-2Z)²/A ± δ
conditions: Bethe-Weizsäcker formula valid for A > 20 approximately
common_traps: binding energy per nucleon (B/A) vs total binding energy B

liquid_drop_model.concept: Treats nucleus as a drop of incompressible nuclear fluid; explains binding energy.
liquid_drop_model.formula: B.E. = avA - asA₂₃ - acZ²/A₁₃ - aa(A-2Z)²/A + δ
conditions: Applies best to heavy nuclei
common_traps: Missing the pairing term sign

nuclear_shell_model.concept: Explains magic numbers and nuclear spin/parity using energy levels.
applications: Predicting ground state spin and parity
conditions: Independent particle approximation
common_traps: Ignoring spin-orbit splitting for higher shells

decay_law.concept: Number of undecayed nuclei decreases exponentially; probability of decay per unit time is constant.
decay_law.formula: N(t) = N₀ e^(-λt); T_{1/2} = ln2/λ; activity A = λN
conditions: constant λ (not affected by chemical/physical environment for nuclear decay)

alpha_decay.concept: Nucleus emits helium-4 nucleus; tunneling through Coulomb barrier.
alpha_decay.formula: ²³⁸U → ²³⁴Th + ⁴He; Q-value = (M_parent - M_daughter - M_alpha)c²
conditions: heavy nuclei (A > 210); Q must be positive
common_traps: alpha particle takes most energy but not all (daughter recoils)

beta_decay.concept: Neutron converts to proton (β⁻) or vice versa (β⁺); emits electron/positron and (anti)neutrino.

photoelectric_and_compton.concept: Quantum nature of light; energy and momentum transfer in photon-electron interactions.

common_traps: Confusing stopping potential with work function

special_relativity_full.concept: Einstein's postulates; transformation of space, time, and mass-energy at high velocities.

blackbody_and_wave_nature.concept: Failure of classical physics; quantization of energy and wave-particle duality.
conditions: Thermal equilibrium
common_traps: Confusing Rayleigh-Jeans with Planck limit

kcl.concept: Sum of currents at any node = 0; conservation of charge.
kcl.formula: Σ Iᵢₙ = Σ Iₒᵤₜ at node

kvl.concept: Sum of voltage drops around any closed loop = 0; conservation of energy.
conditions: quasi-static; neglects EM radiation effects

thevenin_norton_equivalents.concept: Any linear network seen from two terminals equivalent to voltage source + series resistance (Thevenin) or current source + parallel resistance (Norton).
thevenin_norton_equivalents.formula: V_th = open-circuit voltage; R_th = resistance with sources killed; I_N = V_th/R_th
conditions: only for linear networks
common_traps: 'killing' sources: voltage source → short, current source → open

impedance.concept: Complex generalization of resistance to sinusoidal AC; Z = R + jX.
impedance.formula: Z_R = R; Z_L = jωL; Z_C = 1/jωC = -j/ωC; Z_total in series: sum; parallel: reciprocal sum
conditions: sinusoidal steady state; linear elements

resonance_in_rlc.concept: At resonance, impedance purely real; current maximum (series) or minimum (parallel).

conditions: sinusoidal excitation; linear RLC
common_traps: Q definition differs for series and parallel circuits

bjt.concept: Bipolar junction transistor: current-controlled device; small base current controls large collector current.
bjt.formula: IC = βIB; VCE = VCC - IC RC; β = hFE (current gain, typically 50-300)

ideal_opamp.concept: Ideal op-amp has infinite gain, infinite input impedance, zero output impedance; virtual short principle.
ideal_opamp.formula: V+ = V- (virtual short when feedback present); Vout = A(V+ - V-); A → ∞

inverting_amplifier.concept: Output inverted and amplified; gain set by resistor ratio.

common_traps: negative sign (inverting); input impedance is Rin, not infinite

logic_gates.concept: Binary logic operations; outputs determined by Boolean function of inputs.

demorgans_theorem.concept: Duality theorem: complement of AND equals OR of complements, and vice versa.

semiconductor_physics_full.concept: Band structure, carrier statistics, and transport in intrinsic and doped semiconductors.

transistors_and_biasing.concept: Three-terminal devices used for switching and amplification.

sequential_digital_electronics.concept: Circuits with memory elements that depend on previous states.

common_traps: JK Flip-flop race around condition

bravais_lattices.concept: 14 distinct Bravais lattice types in 3D; basis of atoms added to lattice points gives crystal structure.
bravais_lattices.formula: Lattice vectors: a, b, c; primitive cell volume V = a·(b×c)
conditions: periodic structure; translational symmetry
common_traps: confusing Bravais lattice (points) with crystal structure (lattice + basis)

miller_indices.concept: Integer notation for crystal planes; (hkl) plane intercepts axes at a/h, b/k, c/l.

xray_diffraction_and_braggs_law.concept: Constructive interference from crystal planes when Bragg condition satisfied.

common_traps: θ is glancing angle (from plane), not from normal; factor 2

reciprocal_lattice.concept: Fourier transform of the direct lattice; essential for diffraction and band theory.
conditions: Periodic crystal lattice
common_traps: Confusing units (1/length)

intrinsic_semiconductor.concept: Pure semiconductor with equal electron and hole concentrations; conductivity increases with T.
intrinsic_semiconductor.formula: n = p = nᵢ = √(NcNv) e^(-Eg/2kT); conductivity σ = nᵢe(μe + μh)
components: effective density of states Nc, Nv
conditions: thermal equilibrium; no impurities

extrinsic_semiconductor.concept: Doped semiconductor; n-type (donors) or p-type (acceptors) dominant carriers.
extrinsic_semiconductor.formula: n-type: n ≈ N_D; p = nᵢ²/N_D; Fermi level near conduction band

pn_junction.concept: Interface between p and n semiconductors; depletion region with built-in potential.

specific_heat_models.concept: Classical (Dulong-Petit) vs Quantum (Einstein, Debye) models of lattice vibrations.
specific_heat_models.formula: Cv (Debye) ∝ T³ at low T; Cv ∝ 3R at high T

free_electron_model.concept: Electrons treated as a gas of non-interacting particles in a box.

common_traps: Overestimating conductivity at high T

kronig_penney_model.concept: Explains formation of energy bands and gaps using periodic potential.
kronig_penney_model.formula: P (sin αa / αa) + cos αa = cos ka
conditions: 1D periodic delta-function potential
common_traps: Complex math in solving transcendental eq

magnetism_in_solids.concept: Origin of atomic moments and their collective behavior in solids.

superconductivity_core.concept: Zero resistance and perfect diamagnetism at low temperatures.
conditions: Critical temperature Tc

dot_and_cross_products.concept: Dot product gives scalar projection; cross product gives perpendicular vector with magnitude |A||B|sinθ.
conditions: right-hand coordinate system for cross product
common_traps: A×B = -B×A (anticommutative)

vector_identities.concept: Algebraic identities involving combinations of gradient, divergence, curl; used to simplify field equations.

common_traps: ∇²A is vector Laplacian (not scalar applied componentwise in non-Cartesian coords)

covariant_derivative.concept: Generalization of partial derivative to curved space; accounts for basis vector variation.

common_traps: Christoffel symbols are not tensors; Γ=0 in flat space Cartesian but not spherical coords

diagonalization_and_spectral_theorem.concept: Normal matrices (includes Hermitian, unitary) can be diagonalized by unitary transformation.
diagonalization_and_spectral_theorem.formula: A = UDU†; D = diag(λ₁,...,λₙ); U columns are orthonormal eigenvectors
conditions: only normal matrices diagonalizable by unitary; general matrices use Jordan form
common_traps: non-normal matrix may not be diagonalizable (requires Jordan normal form)

cayley_hamilton_theorem.concept: Every square matrix satisfies its own characteristic equation.
cayley_hamilton_theorem.formula: If p(λ) = det(A - λI) = 0 is characteristic polynomial, then p(A) = 0
conditions: valid for all square matrices
common_traps: minimal polynomial may have lower degree than characteristic polynomial

discrete_groups.concept: Set with binary operation satisfying closure, associativity, identity, inverse; finite order groups.
discrete_groups.formula: Group axioms: e∈G; a∘b∈G; (a∘b)∘c=a∘(b∘c); a∘e=a; a∘a⁻¹=e
conditions: group operation must satisfy all four axioms
common_traps: abelian vs non-abelian groups; order of elements vs order of group

lie_groups_and_lie_algebras.concept: Continuous symmetry groups; generators satisfy commutation relations (Lie algebra).
lie_groups_and_lie_algebras.formula: [Jᵢ,Jⱼ] = iεᵢⱼₖJₖ (rotation group SO(3)); SU(2) isomorphic to SO(3) Lie algebra
conditions: generators Hermitian for unitary representations
common_traps: SU(2) and SO(3) same Lie algebra but different global structure (spinors vs vectors)

real_integral_evaluation.concept: Use residue theorem with appropriate contours to evaluate definite real integrals.
real_integral_evaluation.formula: ∫₋∞^∞ f(x)dx = 2πi Σ Res(f,zₖ) for poles in upper half plane
conditions: f(z)→0 sufficiently fast as |z|→∞ (Jordan's lemma)
common_traps: poles exactly on real axis require indented contour (contribution πi·Res)

dispersion_relations.concept: Kramers-Kronig relations connect real and imaginary parts of causal response functions.
conditions: causal system (response vanishes before perturbation)
common_traps: principal value prescription essential at singular point

greens_functions.concept: Impulse response function G(r,r') solving LG = δ(r-r'); solution by convolution.
conditions: linear operator L; boundary conditions must be incorporated
common_traps: Green's function depends on boundary conditions, not just operator

separation_of_variables.concept: Assume product form solution; reduces PDE to ODEs for each variable.
conditions: linear PDE with separable geometry and BCs
common_traps: separation constant must be chosen to satisfy boundary conditions, not arbitrary

wave_equation.concept: PDE governing propagation of waves; solutions are traveling and standing waves.
conditions: linear wave equation; no dispersion in homogeneous medium
common_traps: d'Alembert solution for infinite domain; different form for bounded domain

diffusion_equation.concept: PDE governing heat conduction and diffusion; parabolic type.
diffusion_equation.formula: ∂u/∂t = D∇²u; solution via Fourier transform or separation of variables
conditions: linear; first order in time unlike wave equation (second order)
common_traps: diffusion is irreversible (arrow of time); wave equation is reversible

generating_functions.concept: Functions relating old and new canonical coordinates; four types (F1-F4) depending on variables.
conditions: transformation must preserve Hamilton's equations form (symplectic structure)
common_traps: different generating function types have different sign conventions

hamilton_jacobi_theory.concept: PDE for Hamilton's principal function S; complete integral gives complete solution of equations of motion.
hamilton_jacobi_theory.formula: H(q, ∂S/∂q, t) + ∂S/∂t = 0; S = ∫L dt (action along classical path)
conditions: separability of H-J equation required for complete integral
common_traps: S is not the Lagrangian; it is the action integral

action_angle_variables.concept: For integrable systems, canonical transformation to variables where H = H(J) only; J conserved.
action_angle_variables.formula: J = (1/2π)∮ p dq (action variable); θ̇ = ∂H/∂J = ν(J) (angle variable evolves uniformly)
conditions: fully integrable system with n conserved quantities for n DOF
common_traps: action-angle variables only exist for integrable systems; most systems not integrable

normal_mode_analysis.concept: Systematic diagonalization of coupled oscillator problem using mass and stiffness matrices.
normal_mode_analysis.formula: T = (1/2)q̇ᵀMq̇; V = (1/2)qᵀKq; eigenvalue problem: det(K - ω²M) = 0
components: orthogonality of modes (with respect to M)
conditions: small oscillations about stable equilibrium; K positive definite
common_traps: orthogonality of normal modes is with respect to mass matrix M, not identity

classical_chaos.concept: Sensitive dependence on initial conditions; deterministic yet unpredictable long-term behavior.
classical_chaos.formula: Lyapunov exponent λ: |δx(t)| ~ |δx(0)|e^(λt); λ > 0 for chaos
conditions: nonlinear system; chaos cannot occur in 1D or 2D autonomous Hamiltonian systems
common_traps: chaos ≠ randomness; chaotic systems are fully deterministic

hilbert_space.concept: Complete inner product space; quantum states are normalized vectors; observables are self-adjoint operators.
hilbert_space.formula: ⟨ψ|ψ⟩ = 1; Stone-von Neumann theorem; spectral theorem for self-adjoint operators
conditions: separable Hilbert space for countable basis; rigged Hilbert space for continuous spectrum
common_traps: position/momentum eigenstates not in L² (only in rigged Hilbert space)

density_matrix.concept: Most general quantum state description; pure state: ρ = |ψ⟩⟨ψ|; mixed state: ρ = Σpᵢ|ψᵢ⟩⟨ψᵢ|.
conditions: ρ Hermitian, positive semidefinite, trace 1
common_traps: pure state has Tr(ρ²)=1; mixed state has Tr(ρ²)<1 (not equal)

born_approximation.concept: First-order perturbative treatment of scattering from weak potential; valid when potential small compared to kinetic energy.
conditions: V << E (kinetic energy); or large k (high energy)
common_traps: Born approximation fails for strong potentials and low energies

partial_wave_analysis.concept: Decompose scattering amplitude into contributions from different angular momenta (partial waves).
conditions: spherically symmetric potential; valid for any energy
common_traps: only low-l partial waves important at low energy (ka << 1, s-wave dominates)

lippmann_schwinger_equation.concept: Integral equation for scattering state; incorporates correct boundary conditions.
conditions: +iε for outgoing waves; -iε for incoming
common_traps: iε prescription essential to get correct boundary conditions

symmetrization_and_antisymmetrization.concept: Bosons: symmetric wavefunction under exchange; fermions: antisymmetric (Pauli exclusion).
conditions: only for truly identical particles (same species)
common_traps: two-particle distinguishable: 4 states; bosons: 3 states; fermions: only 1 state for opposite spins

wkb_approximation.concept: Semiclassical approximation; valid when de Broglie wavelength varies slowly compared to itself.
conditions: |dλ/dx| << 1 where λ = h/p; breaks down at classical turning points
common_traps: WKB wavefunction diverges at turning points; must use connection formulas

klein_gordon_equation.concept: Relativistic wave equation for spin-0 particles; second order in time.
conditions: relativistic; fails for fermions (Dirac equation needed for spin-1/2)
common_traps: Klein-Gordon has negative probability density (problem resolved only in QFT)

dirac_equation.concept: First-order relativistic equation for spin-1/2 particles; automatically predicts spin and antiparticles.
conditions: relativistic spin-1/2 particles; Lorentz covariant
common_traps: 4 components: 2 spin states × 2 (particle/antiparticle), not 4 spatial components

ising_model.concept: Lattice model with nearest-neighbor spin interactions; exhibits ferromagnetic phase transition.
ising_model.formula: H = -J Σ_{⟨ij⟩} SᵢSⱼ - μB Σᵢ Sᵢ; Tc exists in 2D and above (Onsager solution for 2D square lattice)
conditions: no exact solution in 3D; 1D Ising has no phase transition at T>0
common_traps: 1D Ising has no finite-T phase transition; 2D does (Onsager)

landau_theory.concept: Phenomenological theory of phase transitions using order parameter; free energy expanded in powers of order parameter.
landau_theory.formula: F = F₀ + a(T-Tc)φ² + bφ⁴ + ...; min F: φ=0 (T>Tc), φ=±√(a(Tc-T)/2b) (T<Tc)
conditions: valid near Tc; breaks down in critical region (fluctuations important)
common_traps: Landau mean-field exponents differ from true (Ising) critical exponents due to fluctuations

critical_exponents.concept: Power-law behavior of thermodynamic quantities near critical point; universal (independent of microscopic details).
conditions: near critical point; scaling hypothesis valid
common_traps: mean-field exponents: β=1/2, γ=1, ν=1/2 are modified by fluctuations in low dimensions

fluctuation_dissipation_theorem.concept: Response of system to external perturbation related to spontaneous equilibrium fluctuations.
conditions: linear response; near thermal equilibrium
common_traps: theorem valid only near equilibrium; not for driven systems far from equilibrium

brownian_motion.concept: Random motion of particle due to thermal fluctuations; described by Langevin equation.
conditions: overdamped limit common; inertia negligible for small particles in liquid
common_traps: D = kT/γ not kT/m; friction and diffusion related by fluctuation-dissipation

larmor_formula.concept: Power radiated by non-relativistic accelerating charge proportional to acceleration squared.
conditions: non-relativistic v << c; point charge
common_traps: relativistic extension requires Liénard formula (replaces a² with relativistic expression)

radiation_fields.concept: Far-field (radiation zone) fields fall as 1/r and carry energy to infinity.
components: near field (1/r² Coulomb) vs radiation field (1/r)
conditions: radiation zone r >> wavelength >> source size
common_traps: near field and radiation field have different distance dependences; only radiation field important at large r

electric_dipole_radiation.concept: Leading radiation mechanism for oscillating charge distribution; power ∝ ω⁴|p̈|².
conditions: wavelength >> source size (dipole approximation)
common_traps: P ∝ ω⁴, not ω²; this gives Rayleigh scattering blue sky

time_translation_symmetry.concept: Invariance of L under t → t + ε implies energy conservation; H = const when ∂L/∂t = 0.
time_translation_symmetry.formula: E = Σ p_iq̇ᵢ - L = H; dH/dt = -∂L/∂t
applications: energy conservation in all closed systems
conditions: ∂L/∂t = 0 required for energy conservation
common_traps: explicitly time-dependent Lagrangian does not conserve energy (H not constant)

gauge_symmetry.concept: U(1) gauge invariance of electrodynamics; local phase transformation requires electromagnetic field.
gauge_symmetry.formula: ψ → e^(iqΛ/ℏ)ψ; A_μ → A_μ + ∂_μΛ; invariant under combined transformation
conditions: exact symmetry of nature; basis of all standard model gauge theories
common_traps: only local (position-dependent) phase invariance requires gauge field; global phase symmetry gives charge conservation only

poincare_sections.concept: Stroboscopic cross-section of phase space trajectory; reveals structure of orbits.
poincare_sections.formula: Sample trajectory when q₁ = const (or at period of driving); plot remaining phase space coords
conditions: autonomous system reduced by one degree by fixing one coordinate
common_traps: Poincaré section dimension is n-1 for n-dimensional phase space

measurement_postulate.concept: Measurement of observable A on state |ψ⟩ yields eigenvalue aₙ with probability |⟨aₙ|ψ⟩|²; state collapses to |aₙ⟩.
conditions: ideal (projective) measurement; approximate for realistic measurements (POVMs)
common_traps: measurement of commuting observables can be simultaneous; non-commuting cannot

epr_and_entanglement.concept: Entangled states have correlations stronger than any classical model; violate Bell inequalities.
conditions: entanglement is basis-independent property of quantum states
common_traps: entanglement cannot be used for faster-than-light communication

creation_and_annihilation_operators.concept: Algebraic description of many-particle quantum systems; operators add/remove particles.
creation_and_annihilation_operators.formula: Bosons: [aₖ, aₖ'†] = δₖₖ'; Fermions: {cₖ, cₖ'†} = δₖₖ'; N̂ₖ = aₖ†aₖ
conditions: identical particles; Fock space as direct sum of n-particle spaces
common_traps: bosons commute; fermions anticommute (fundamental difference)

hamiltonian_in_second_quantization.concept: One-body and two-body Hamiltonians written using creation/annihilation operators; automatically symmetrized.
hamiltonian_in_second_quantization.formula: H = Σₖₗ tₖₗ cₖ†cₗ + (1/2)Σₖₗₘₙ Vₖₗₘₙ cₖ†cₗ†cₙcₘ
conditions: correct operator ordering critical; anticommutation enforces antisymmetry automatically
common_traps: index ordering in two-body term; minus signs from anticommutation

feynman_path_integral.concept: Quantum amplitude expressed as sum over all paths; each path weighted by e^(iS/ℏ).
conditions: equivalent to Schrödinger equation; basis of QFT
common_traps: classical path dominates when S >> ℏ (classical limit); quantum corrections from fluctuations

semiclassical_expansion.concept: Expand path integral around classical path; leading quantum correction is Gaussian integral over fluctuations.
conditions: S_cl >> ℏ for semiclassical approximation to be valid
common_traps: prefactor A (fluctuation determinant) often important and non-trivial

qubits_and_quantum_gates.concept: Qubit is two-state quantum system; quantum gates are unitary operations on qubits.
conditions: coherence must be maintained; decoherence destroys quantum advantage
common_traps: cannot clone an unknown quantum state (no-cloning theorem)

bloch_theorem.concept: Wavefunction in periodic potential can be written as plane wave times periodic function.
bloch_theorem.formula: ψₙₖ(r) = uₙₖ(r)e^(ik·r); uₙₖ(r+R) = uₙₖ(r) for lattice vector R
conditions: perfect periodic potential; no disorder
common_traps: k is crystal (quasi) momentum, not true momentum; ranges over 1st Brillouin zone

tight_binding_model.concept: Electronic bands from overlap of atomic orbitals; simple model for band dispersion.
tight_binding_model.formula: E(k) = ε₀ - 2t cos(ka) (1D chain); t is hopping integral
conditions: well-localized atomic orbitals; small overlap (tight binding valid)
common_traps: bandwidth increases with overlap (larger t); opposite to free electron (wider band for smaller lattice)

fermi_surface.concept: Surface of constant energy E_F in k-space; determines electronic properties of metals.
fermi_surface.formula: E(k_F) = E_F; shape from band dispersion; topology affects transport
conditions: T << T_F (low temperature); Fermi liquid theory validity
common_traps: Fermi surface exists only for metals; insulators/semiconductors have no crossing at E_F

bcs_theory_basics.concept: Phonon-mediated attractive interaction between electrons pairs them into Cooper pairs; condensate has superconducting gap.
conditions: conventional s-wave pairing; N(0)V << 1 (weak coupling)
common_traps: Tc ≠ Δ/k; Tc = 0.57Δ/k (ratio 2Δ/kTc ≈ 3.52 in BCS)

meissner_effect.concept: Perfect diamagnetism in superconductor; magnetic field expelled from bulk (not just due to perfect conductivity).
meissner_effect.formula: B = 0 inside; London equations: ∇×J = -(1/μ₀λ_L²)B; λ_L = √(m/μ₀nse²) (London penetration depth)
components: type I vs type II (Abrikosov vortices)
conditions: below Tc and below critical field Hc (type I) or Hc2 (type II)
common_traps: Meissner effect (B=0) is distinct from perfect conductivity (dB/dt=0)

integer_quantum_hall_effect.concept: Hall conductance quantized in integer multiples of e²/h; robust topological phenomenon.
integer_quantum_hall_effect.formula: σxy = ν e²/h; ν integer; Rxy = h/νe² (quantum resistance standard)
conditions: low temperature; high magnetic field; 2D electron gas
common_traps: IQHE requires disorder for plateau formation (disorder localizes bulk states)

liquid_drop_model.concept: Nucleus treated as incompressible liquid drop; explains binding energy trends and fission.
liquid_drop_model.formula: B = aᵥA - aₛA^(2/3) - a_C Z(Z-1)/A^(1/3) - aₐ(A-2Z)²/A ± δ/√A
conditions: valid for A > 20; fails near magic numbers (shell effects)
common_traps: liquid drop cannot explain magic numbers; needs shell model

nuclear_shell_model.concept: Nucleons move in mean field potential; magic numbers from spin-orbit splitting of shells.
conditions: single-particle approximation; mean field
common_traps: magic numbers above 20 require spin-orbit coupling to reproduce; H.O. alone gives wrong ordering

standard_model_structure.concept: SU(3)×SU(2)×U(1) gauge theory; quarks, leptons, gauge bosons, Higgs.
conditions: perturbative QCD valid at high energy; strong coupling at low energy (confinement)
common_traps: gravity not included in Standard Model; neutrino masses require beyond-SM physics

feynman_diagrams_basics.concept: Pictorial representation of perturbation theory terms; lines = propagators, vertices = interactions.
feynman_diagrams_basics.formula: Amplitude M from diagram rules; σ ∝ |M|²; vertex factor ∝ coupling constant g
conditions: perturbation theory valid when coupling g << 1; QED fine (α≈1/137); QCD at high E
common_traps: virtual particles do not satisfy E²=p²c²+m²c⁴; they are off-shell

buckingham_pi_theorem.concept: Physical equation with n variables and k independent dimensions can be written with n-k dimensionless groups.
buckingham_pi_theorem.formula: n variables, k dimensions → n-k dimensionless Π groups
components: fundamental dimensions (M, L, T, Θ, I...)
conditions: all relevant variables must be identified
common_traps: missing a relevant variable invalidates result

order_of_magnitude_estimation.concept: Fermi estimation: use known quantities and scaling to estimate unknowns to within factor of 10.
order_of_magnitude_estimation.formula: Express answer as 10^n with n estimated from constituent factors
conditions: accuracy to factor of 10 sufficient; identify dominant physics
common_traps: confusing order of magnitude with factor of 2-3 precision

spectroscopy.concept: Study of interaction of radiation with matter; reveals energy level structure.
spectroscopy.formula: E = hν = hc/λ; resolution R = λ/δλ = ν/δν
conditions: electric dipole selection rules determine allowed transitions
common_traps: Doppler broadening ∝ T^(1/2) while natural linewidth is temperature-independent

low_temperature_physics.concept: Techniques to reach temperatures from mK to nK; cryostats, dilution refrigerators.
low_temperature_physics.formula: Carnot COP = T_cold/(T_hot - T_cold); ³He-⁴He dilution: T_min ~ 10 mK
conditions: each cooling technique has a lower temperature limit
common_traps: dilution refrigerator operates continuously (not adiabatic); adiabatic demagnetization is one-shot

vacuum_technology.concept: Achieving and maintaining low-pressure environment for particle physics and surface science experiments.
vacuum_technology.formula: Mean free path λ = kT/(√2 πd²P); high vacuum: λ >> chamber size
conditions: UHV (< 10⁻⁹ mbar) required for surface-sensitive experiments
common_traps: outgassing of chamber walls limits ultimate vacuum; must bake out
